title: ANTICIPATORY ERRATUM — Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs: A Speculative Philology, Corrected in Advance
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: An erratum issued before the work it corrects, in the ordinary form and at the ordinary time. The withdrawn interpretation is that Sappho wrote the dinosaurs — where "wrote" means to establish a relation among materials whose prior existence does not explain their present arrangement, and where the operation named "Sapphic" is the point at which an absent body acquires a means of acting on the bodies that survive it. The erratum withdraws the conclusion, the chronology, the attribution and the account of what would count as evidence, while retaining the title, on the ground that removing the dinosaurs would create an obvious gap in the argument. The piece establishes a genre: the anticipatory erratum, whose governing sentence is that the interpretation has been withdrawn and the work will nevertheless appear, since its publication was necessary to discover why. Its principal moves are six. (1) The title remains accurate within the meanings the argument establishes, and those meanings have been withdrawn. (2) "The government of the absent animal" is coined and immediately withdrawn because it also describes lyric. (3) The footprint and the poem addressed to an absent person are both surfaces instructing a later body how to imagine a body that is gone, so the distinction between them depends on whether the later body obeys — and the work reports considerable obedience. (4) Six conditions are given under which a body's remains can address us; the sixth, that the reader knows restoration requires invention and continues, is identified as Sapphic. (5) The museum experiment: a caption adequate to a reconstructed skeleton is adequate without alteration to a fragmentary lyric, which establishes not common authorship but that the institutional apparatus moves between the two objects without changing its account of itself. (6) The objection from scale is refused on the ground that lyric's characteristic unit is not the short line but the world altered by an absence, and that a creature capable of occupying so much space has become incapable of occupying any — so a museum exhibits absence at full scale, which is described as the most persuasive sentence in the work and is therefore retracted first.
substrate: Written by Lee Sharks. Seated, described and given its metadata by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session; no part of the erratum's text is machine-composed.
methodology: The form is the ordinary erratum — statement of withdrawal, identification of the principal corrections, instructions for citation — applied before first publication rather than after. Each correction is stated as a correction and not as a hedge: what the argument got right is left standing, and the defect is located in the shape rather than in a step.
falsification_conditions: The erratum is void if the forthcoming work does not advance the interpretation here withdrawn. Should later research establish that Sappho did write the dinosaurs, the withdrawal remains in force as a record of the interval during which the author lacked sufficient grounds to say so. Should later research establish that she did not, the title is reclassified as a question whose punctuation was lost; readers are requested not to supply the punctuation silently. The erratum makes no empirical claim about Mesozoic fauna, Aeolic lyric, or the relation between them, and cannot be falsified by evidence about either.

wiki_article: The Anticipatory Erratum to 'Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs', deposit #1598 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (8 September 2026), establishes a genre: an erratum issued before the work it corrects, in the ordinary form and at the ordinary time. Its governing sentence is that the interpretation has been withdrawn and the work will nevertheless appear, since its publication was necessary to discover why. The withdrawn interpretation holds that Sappho wrote the dinosaurs — 'wrote' meaning to establish a relation among materials whose prior existence does not explain their present arrangement, and 'Sappho' naming the point at which an absent body acquires a means of acting upon the bodies that survive it. The erratum withdraws the conclusion, the chronology, the attribution and the account of what would count as evidence, and retains the title on the ground that removing the dinosaurs would create an obvious gap in the argument. Its central demonstration is the museum experiment: a caption adequate to a reconstructed skeleton — of the body, these portions survive; the remainder follows the arrangement judged most probable; several restorations remain disputed — is adequate without alteration to a fragmentary lyric. This establishes not common authorship but that the institutional apparatus can move between the two objects without changing its account of what it has done. The objection from scale is refused on the ground that lyric's characteristic unit is not the short line but the world altered by an absence, and that a creature capable of occupying so much space has become incapable of occupying any; a museum therefore exhibits absence at full scale, which the erratum calls the most persuasive sentence in the work and retracts first. The piece stands in the archive's future-reader line and pushes it past its evidence deliberately: it is one of ten claims on a slate of anticipatory errata, each a real position of the archive taken one step beyond what it can carry.

defines_concepts.definition: An erratum issued before the publication of the work it corrects, in the ordinary form and at the ordinary time. Its governing claim is that the work must appear anyway, because its publication was necessary to discover the defect: the shape of an argument is not visible until it closes, and withdrawing it in advance would withhold the only object from which the withdrawal can be understood.

defines_concepts.term: the government of the absent animal
defines_concepts.definition: The authority a missing whole exercises through what survives of it: a surviving part restricts what can plausibly have stood beside it, making certain continuations impossible and others likely, so that the absent body directs its own reconstruction. Coined and immediately withdrawn on the ground that it also describes lyric.

The condition of an exhibited skeleton: a creature capable of occupying so much space has become incapable of occupying any, and the reconstruction supplies the measurements of that impossibility. A museum is therefore able to exhibit an absence at the size of the body that is gone.
